text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Cabinet decided on December 24 to reduce the tax-exempted minimum for residents' income tax to 21 lats from 25. The new rate will take effect from January 1, 1997.
- The introduction of compulsory motor vehicle insurance has been postponed by the government to May 1 next year from the planned January 1.
- Cabinet approved regulations for visa-free travel for Danes entering Latvia, effective from January 1, 1997.

- The Alcohol Monopoly Board will be re-organised into the Board of Excise-taxed Goods as of January 1. The board will be responsible for issuing licences to businesses dealing in excise goods. The collection of the alcohol tax, in turn, will be carried out by the State Revenue Service.
- Riga City Council has decided to replace old road-signs in the next three years at an estimated costs of 595,600 lats.
